The discussion of al-buruj has already preceded at the explanation of His saying: ﴿He has placed in the sky buruj﴾ [al-Furqan: 61]. al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: they are the stars, and the meaning is: "By the sky containing the stars."

'Ikrimah and Mujahid also said: they are palaces in the sky.

al-Minhal ibn 'Amr said: "containing a good creation."

Abu 'Ubaydah, Yahya ibn Salam and others said: they are the stations (manazil) for the planets, and they are twelve buruj for twelve planets: Aries (al-Hamal), Taurus (al-Thawr), Gemini (al-Jawza'), Cancer (al-Saratan), Leo (al-Asad), Virgo (al-Sunbulah), Libra (al-Mizan), Scorpio (al-'Aqrab), Sagittarius (al-Qaws), Capricorn (al-Jadi), Aquarius (al-Dalw), and Pisces (al-Hut).

In the language of the Arabs, al-buruj means palaces, and from it is His saying: ﴿Even if you were in towers built up high﴾ [al-Nisa': 78]. The stations of these stars were likened to palaces because they dwell in them. It was said: they are the gates of the sky. It was said: they are the stations of the moon. The origin of al-burj is manifestation, (p-1604) and they were named so because of their visibility.

And "the promised day" means the day that was promised, which is the Day of Resurrection.

al-Wahidi said: according to the saying of all the exegetes, "witness and witnessed": the witness (al-shahid) is whoever attends on that day from among the creatures, i.e., who is present therein, and the witnessed (al-mashhud) is what is witnessed on that day of wonders. A group of the Companions and the Successors held that the witness is the day of Friday, and that it bears witness over every doer for what he did therein, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah, because people witness the Hajj season therein and the angels attend it.

al-Wahidi said: this is the saying of the majority.

al-Qushayri related from Ibn 'Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr that the witness is the day of al-Adha.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: the witness is the day of al-Tarwiyah, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah.

al-Nakha'i said: the witness is the day of 'Arafah, and the witnessed is the day of al-Nahr. It was also said: the witness is Allah, Glorified is He.

al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said this, citing His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as witness﴾ [al-Fath: 28], and His saying: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest as testimony?" Say: "Allah is witness between me and you"﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. It was also said: the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), citing His saying: ﴿So how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these?﴾ [al-Nisa': 41], and His saying: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ [al-Ahzab: 45], and His saying: ﴿And the Messenger will be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. It was also said: the witness is all the prophets, citing His saying: ﴿So how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness﴾. It was also said: it is Jesus son of Mary, citing His saying: ﴿And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 117]. The witnessed, according to these three sayings, is either the nation of Muhammad, or the nations of the prophets, or the nation of Jesus.

It was said: the witness is Adam and the witnessed is his offspring.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: the witness is the human being, citing His saying: ﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra': 14]. Mujahid said: its limbs, citing His saying: ﴿On the Day when their tongues and their hands and their feet will testify against them as to what they used to do﴾ [al-Nur: 24]. al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: the witness is this nation, and the witnessed is the rest of the nations, citing His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. It was said: the witness is the guardian angels (al-hafazah) and the witnessed is the children of Adam. It was said: the days and nights.

It was said: the witness is the creation, who bear witness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of His oneness, and the one witnessed to as One is Allah, Glorified is He. The explanation of what has come in the interpretation of the witness and the witnessed, and the statement of what is the truth, will come, Allah willing.

﴿The companions of the trench were killed﴾. This is the response to the oath, and the lam in it is implied, and this is the apparent view; al-Farra' and others held this. It was said its estimate is: "Indeed, were killed," so the lam and "qad" were omitted, and on this the sentence is informative. The apparent view is that it is supplicatory (du'a'iyyah), because the meaning of "qutila" is "la'ana" (was cursed).

al-Wahidi said: according to the consensus, and a supplicatory sentence cannot be the response to an oath. It was said the response is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who tormented the believing men and believing women...﴾. It was said it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾, and this is the view of al-Mubarrad, though it was objected to on account of the long separation. It was said it is an estimated clause indicated by His saying "qutila ashab al-ukhdud," as if He said: "I swear by these things that the disbelievers of Quraysh are cursed as the companions of the trench were cursed." It was said the estimate of the response is: "You will surely be resurrected," and Ibn al-Anbari chose this.

Abu Hatim al-Sijistani and also Ibn al-Anbari said: there is inversion and displacement in the speech: i.e., "The companions of the trench were killed, and [by] the sky containing the buruj." This was objected to on the ground that it is not permissible to say: "By Allah, Zayd stood."

al-Ukhdud: a great long cleft in the earth like a trench; its plural is akhadid. From it comes al-khadd (cheek), for the channels of tears, and al-mikhaddah (pillow), because the cheek is placed upon it. It is said "takhadadda wajh al-rajul" when furrows of boils appear in a man's face. From it is the saying of Tarafah:

"And a face as if the sun had cast its garment upon it, clear of complexion, not furrowed."

The explanation of the hadith of the companions of the trench will come, Allah willing.

The majority read "al-nari dhati al-waqud" with the genitive "al-nar," as a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimal) from "al-ukhdud," because the trench includes it. "Dhat al-waqud" is an adjective of it, that it is a great fire. al-Waqud is the firewood with which it is kindled. It was said it is a substitute of whole from whole (badal kull min kull), not a substitute of inclusion.

It was said that "al-nar" is in the genitive by attraction (al-jiwar); thus Makki related from the Kufans.

The majority read the waw in "al-waqud" with a fatha, while Qatadah, Abu Raja' and Nasr ibn 'Asim read it with a damma.

Ashhab al-'Uqayli, Abu Haywah, Abu al-Simak al-'Adawi, Ibn al-Sumayfa' and 'Isa read "al-nar" in the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject: i.e., "it is the fire," or as the subject of an omitted verb: i.e., "the fire burned them."

﴿When they were sitting over it﴾. The operator of the adverbial phrase is "qutila": i.e., they were cursed when they encircled the fire, sitting at what is close to it and near to it.

Muqatil said: meaning, sitting near the fire, presenting them with disbelief.

Mujahid said: they were sitting on chairs beside the trench.

﴿And they, of what they did to the believers, were witnesses﴾: i.e., those who dug the trench, who were the king and his companions, were witnesses to what they did to the believers of presenting them to the fire so that they would return to their religion. "Witnesses" means present, or some of them bear witness to others before the king that he did not fall short in what he was commanded.

It was said they bear witness to what they did on the Day of Resurrection, then their tongues, hands and feet will testify against them.

It was said "ala" is in the sense of "ma'a" (with), and the estimate is: "and they, with what they did to the believers, were witnesses."

al-Zajjaj said: Allah informed of the story of a people whose insight and true faith reached the point that they endured being burned with fire for the sake of Allah.

﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾: i.e., they did not object to them nor find fault with them except that they affirmed belief in Allah, the Victorious, the One praised in every state.

al-Zajjaj said: they did not object to them for any sin except their faith. This is like His saying: ﴿Do you resent us except that we believed in Allah﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 59]. This is an emphasis of praise by means of what resembles blame, as in the saying of the poet:

"There is no fault in them except that the guest with them / is distant from family, homeland and kin."

And another said:

"There is no fault in her except the squint of her eye, / as with the noble birds, the squint of whose eyes is their beauty."

al-Jumhur read "naqamu" with a fatha on the nun, while Abu Haywah read it with a kasra, and the eloquent is the fatha.

Then Glorified is He described Himself with what indicates greatness and majesty, saying: ﴿To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. And whoever has this status is worthy that He be believed in and made one. ﴿And Allah, over all things, is Witness﴾ — regarding their deeds against the believers (p-1605) — nothing is hidden from Him. In this is a severe warning for the companions of the trench, and a promise of good for those believers among them whom they tormented for their religion.

Then Glorified is He explained what He prepared for those who did to the believers what they did of burning, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who tormented the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the burning fire﴾: i.e., they burned them with fire. The Arabs say: "fatantu al-shay'," i.e., I burned it, and "fatantu al-dirham wa-al-dinar" when you put them into fire to see their quality. It is said "dinar maftun," and the goldsmith is called "al-fattan." From it is His saying: ﴿The Day they will be tried over the fire﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 13], i.e., they will be burned. It was also said the meaning of "fatanu al-mu'minin" is they tested them in their religion so that they would turn away from it; "then they did not repent" of their foul deed and turn back from their disbelief and their tormenting; "for them is the punishment of Hell": i.e., for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of Hell because of their disbelief. The sentence is in the place of nominative, as the predicate of "inna," or the predicate is "lahum," and "adhab Jahannam" is raised by it as agent. The fa' is for the subject containing the meaning of a condition. Its abrogation by "inna" does not harm, contrary to al-Akhfash. "And for them is the punishment of the burning": i.e., and for them is another punishment in addition to the punishment of their disbelief, which is the punishment of the burning that they inflicted upon the believers. It was said "al-Hariq" is one of the names of the fire, like "al-Sa'ir." It was said they will be punished in Hell with the zamharir (extreme cold), then they will be punished with the punishment of the burning; the first is punishment by its cold, and the second is punishment by its heat.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: the punishment of the burning, they were afflicted with it in this world, because the fire rose from the trench to the king and his companions and burned them. al-Kalbi also said this.

Then He mentioned what He prepared for the believers who were burned with fire, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. The apparent meaning of the verse is generality, so those burned in the trench for their faith enter into it first and foremost. The meaning is: those who combine faith and righteous deeds ﴿will have gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: i.e., for them, because of faith and righteous deed, are gardens characterized by this attribute.

The manner in which rivers flow beneath the gardens has already been mentioned in more than one place, and we clarified that if "gardens" is meant as trees, then the flowing of rivers beneath them is clear; and if it is meant as the land containing them, then "beneath" is with regard to its visible part, which is the trees, since they cover its courtyard. The reference in His saying "that" is to what has been mentioned before of what Allah prepared for them: i.e., that mentioned is the great triumph, to which no triumph is equal, nor close, nor near. "Triumph" is attaining the sought-after object.

The sentence ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾ is a resumed sentence addressed to the Prophet (ﷺ), explaining what is with Allah, Glorified is He, of recompense for those who disobey Him and forgiveness for those who obey Him: i.e., His seizing of the tyrants and oppressors is severe. Al-batsh is seizing with force, and describing it with severity indicates that it has increased and intensified. A similar statement is His saying: ﴿Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ [Hud: 102].

﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats﴾: i.e., He creates first in this world and restores them alive after death.

Thus said the majority. It was said He originates for the disbelievers the punishment of the burning in this world, then repeats it for them in the Hereafter; Ibn Jarir chose this, but the first is more preferable.

﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Loving﴾: i.e., abundant in forgiveness for the sins of His believing servants, not disgracing them with them; abundant in love for the obedient among His friends.

Mujahid said: "al-wadud" is the one who loves His friends, so it is fa'ul in the sense of fa'il.

Ibn Zayd said: The meaning of al-Wadud is the Merciful.

Al-Mubarrad related from Isma'il al-Qadi that al-Wadud is the one who has no child, and he recited:

"And I ride in the battle, a naked woman, [on a horse] of subdued wing, a mare, a barren one (wadud)."

That is, she has no child for whom she yearns.

It was also said that al-Wadud is in the sense of al-mawdud (the one who is loved): that is, His righteous servants love Him and hold Him dear. So said al-Azhari. He said: "It is also permissible that fa'ul be in the sense of fa'il, meaning that He is loving toward them."

He said: "Both attributes are praise, for if Exalted is His remembrance loves His obedient servants, it is an act of grace from Him; and if His knowing servants love Him, it is because of the generous kindness they have come to recognize from Him."

The majority (al-Jumhur) read "dhu al-'arsh al-majid" with the majid in the nominative (raf'), as an adjective (na't) of "dhu." Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose this reading, and both said: "Because majd (glory) is the utmost in generosity and bounty, and Allah, glorified is He, is the one described by it."

The Kufans, except 'Asim, read it in the genitive (jarr), as an adjective of al-'arsh (the Throne).

He, glorified is He, has described His Throne with generosity (karam), as in the end of Surat al-Mu'minun.

It was also said that it is an adjective of Rabbika (your Lord), and the separation between them does no harm, since they are attributes of Allah, glorified is He.

Makki said: it is a predicate after a predicate, but the first is preferable.

The meaning of "dhu al-'arsh" is "possessor of dominion and authority," as one says: "So-and-so is on the throne of his kingdom." From this is the poet's saying:

"They saw my throne with its two sides broken, and when it was broken, they isolated me."

And the saying of another:

"If they kill you, their thrones have been struck down, by 'Utayba ibn al-Harith ibn Shihab."

It was also said that the intended meaning is the Creator of the Throne.

"Fa'alun li-ma yurid" (Doer of what He intends): that is, of beginning and returning (of creation).

'Ata said: He is not incapable of anything He wills, and nothing He seeks is withheld from Him. The nominative of fa'alun is by being the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada').

Al-Farra' said: it is in the nominative by repetition and resumption (al-tikrar wa'l-istinaf), since it is an absolutely indefinite noun (nakira mahda).

Ibn Jarir said: the nominative of fa'alun, which is an absolutely indefinite noun, is in agreement with the case of al-Ghafur al-Wadud. He said "fa'alun" because what He wills and does is in the utmost abundance.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the report of the disbelieving hosts, saying: "Has there come to you the report of the armies?" The sentence is independent (mustanafa), confirming what preceded of the severity of His seizing, glorified is He, and of His being a Doer of what He intends. In it is consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that is, "Has there come to you, O Muhammad, the report of the disbelieving hosts, who denied their prophets and were arrayed against them?"

Then He specified them, saying: "Pharaoh and Thamud." It is a substitution (badal) for "the armies."

By Pharaoh is meant him and his people, and by Thamud is meant the well-known people. By their report is meant what occurred from them of disbelief and obstinacy, and what befell them of punishment. Their story is well known and its mention has been repeated in the Mighty Book in more than one place. He limited it to these two groups because their matter is famous among the People of the Book and among the polytheist Arabs, and by them He pointed to their likes.

Then He turned away from comparing these disbelievers existing in his time (ﷺ) to those previously mentioned, and made clear that they are worse than them in disbelief and denial, saying: "Nay, those who disbelieve are in denial." That is: nay, these polytheists among the Arabs are in severe denial of you and of what you have brought, and they have not taken warning from those disbelievers who came before them.

"And Allah encompasses them from behind them" (Allah is encompassing of them from behind them): that is, He is able to bring upon them what He brought upon those. Encompassing (ihata) a thing is restraining it from all its sides, so this is a figure of speech for their not escaping, since the one encompassed cannot get away from the one encompassing.

Then He, glorified is He, returned their denial of the Qur'an, saying: "Nay, it is a Glorious Qur'an" (Qur'anun majid): that is, supremely exalted in nobility, generosity and blessing, for it is an exposition of what Allah has legislated for His servants of the rulings of the religion and of this world, and it is not, as they say, poetry, soothsaying, or magic.

"In a Preserved Tablet" (fi lawhin mahfuz): that is, written on a tablet, which is the Mother of the Book, preserved with Allah from the reach of the devils.

The majority read "mahfuzin" in the genitive, as an adjective of "lawh." Nafi' read it in the nominative, as an adjective of "al-Qur'an": that is, "Nay, it is a Glorious Qur'an preserved in a tablet."

The reciters agreed on the fatha of the lam in "lawh," except Yahya ibn Ya'mar and Ibn al-Sumayfa', who read it with a damma.

Muqatil said: the Preserved Tablet is on the right of the Throne.

It was said that by "al-lawh" with a damma on the lam is meant the air above the seventh heaven.

Abu al-Fadl said: "al-luh" with a damma on the lam is air, and Ibn Khalawayh said likewise.

In al-Sihah he said: "al-luh" with a damma is the air between the heaven and the earth.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The buruj are palaces in the sky."

Ibn Mardawayh related from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about "the sky of the buruj," and he said: "The stars." He was asked about His saying: "Who has placed in the sky buruj" [al-Furqan: 61], and he said: "The stars." And about His saying: "In towers built up" [al-Nisa': 78], and he said: "Palaces."

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "And the promised day, and witness and witnessed" [al-Buruj: 2–3], that he said: "The promised day is the Day of Resurrection; the witness is the Day of Friday (Jumu'a); the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa, and it is the Greater Hajj. The Day of Friday, Allah made it a festival for Muhammad and his Ummah, and preferred them thereby over all creation; it is the master of days with Allah, and the most beloved of deeds to Allah are done on it. In it is an hour in which no Muslim servant who prays and asks Allah for good will coincide with it, except that He gives him it."

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witnessed day is the Day of 'Arafa, and the witness is the Day of Friday. The sun has not risen nor set upon a day better than it. In it is an hour in which no believing servant coincides with it, asking Allah for good, except that Allah answers him; and he does not seek refuge from anything except that He protects him from it."

al-Hakim related and authenticated, as did Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi, from Abu Hurayra, raising it: "'And witness and witnessed': he said: The witness is the Day of 'Arafa and the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the promised one, the Day of Resurrection."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib who said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witnessed is the Day of Sacrifice (al-nahr), and the witness is the Day of Friday.

Ibn Jarir and al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh related by the route of Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witness is the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa."

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related from Jubayr ibn Mut'im who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning the verse: "The witness is the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa."

'Abd ibn Humayd related the like from Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Hurayra as a mawquf (companion's) report.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the master of days is Friday, and it is the witness, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa." This is a mursal report from the mursal reports of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.

Ibn Majah, al-Tabarani and Ibn Jarir related from Abu al-Darda' who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Increase your sending of blessings upon me on the Day of Friday, for it is a witnessed day, which the angels witness."

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib regarding the verse that he said: The witness is the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali that a man asked him about His saying: "And witness and witnessed," and he said: "Have you asked anyone before me?" He said: "Yes, I asked Ibn 'Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr, and they said: the Day of Sacrifice and the Day of Friday." He said: "No, but the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ)," then he recited: "And We bring you as a witness over these" [al-Nisa': 41]; "and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection," then he recited: "That is a day on which mankind will be gathered, and that is a witnessed day" [Hud: 103].

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and al-Saghir, and Ibn Mardawayh related from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali regarding the verse that he said: The witness is my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection; then he recited: "Indeed We have sent you as a witness" [al-Ahzab: 45], and "That is a witnessed day."

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related by various routes from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection; then he recited: "That is a day on which mankind will be gathered, and that is a witnessed day" [Hud: 103]. Ibn Jarir also related from him: The witness is Allah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: The witness is Allah.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: The witness is Allah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

I say: These interpretations from the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, have differed, as you see, and likewise the interpretations of the Successors after them differed. Those among them who relied upon verses in which Allah mentions that a thing is a witness or witnessed took that as evidence that this is what is meant by "witness" and "witnessed" in this absolute verse. But that is not an argument by which it is established that the witness and witnessed mentioned in this context are that witness and witnessed mentioned in another verse; otherwise it would follow that His saying here "witness and witnessed" means everything to which the Mighty Book or the Pure Sunna has applied the description of being witnessed or witnessing, and none of what they cited, despite their differing, is more deserving than another, and no one has said so.

If you say: Does the raised report that you mentioned, from the two hadiths of Abu Hurayra, the hadith of Abu Malik, the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im, and the mursal of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, specify this promised day and the witness and witnessed? I say: As for the promised day, these reports which mention it do not differ; rather they agree that it is the Day of Resurrection. As for the witness, in the first hadith of Abu Hurayra it is the Day of Friday; in his second hadith it is the Day of Friday; in the mursal of Sa'id it is the Day of Friday; in his second hadith it is the Day of 'Arafa and the Day of Friday; in the hadith of Abu Malik it is the Day of Friday; in the hadith of Jubayr it is the Day of Friday; in the mursal of Sa'id it is the Day of Friday. These hadiths thus agree upon it, and the addition of the Day of 'Arafa to it in the second hadith of Abu Hurayra does no harm. As for the witnessed, in the first hadith of Abu Hurayra it is the Day of 'Arafa; in his second hadith it is the Day of Resurrection; in the hadith of Abu Malik it is the Day of 'Arafa; in the hadith of Jubayr it is the Day of 'Arafa; likewise in the hadith of Sa'id. Thus it has become determined in these reports that it is the Day of 'Arafa, and these are more preferred than that report in which it is stated to be the Day of Resurrection. From the totality of this results the preference of what the majority of the Companions, the Successors and those after them held: that the witness is the Day of Friday and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa. As for the promised day, we have already mentioned that consensus has occurred that it is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 85, verses 11–22 (part 3 of 3):

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and al-Tabarani narrated from Suhayb that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There was a king among those who came before you, and this king had a soothsayer (kahin) who foretold for him. The soothsayer said to him: 'Look for me a youth who is intelligent and quick-witted, and I will teach him my knowledge, for I fear that I will die and this knowledge will be cut off from you, and there will be no one among you who knows it.' So they searched for a youth fitting his description, and they ordered him to attend the soothsayer and to visit him regularly. The youth kept visiting him. On the youth's path there was a monk (rahib) in a hermitage (sawma'ah), so the youth would ask that monk whenever he passed by him, until the monk informed him. The monk said: 'I only worship Allah.' The youth began to linger with this monk and to be late for the soothsayer, so the soothsayer sent to the youth's family that he was hardly ever present with him. The youth informed the monk of this, and the monk said to him: 'When he asks you, Where were you? say, With my family; and when your family asks you, Where were you? tell them, I was with the soothsayer.'

"While the youth was in this state, he passed by a large crowd of people who had been held up by an animal, which it is said was a lion. The youth took a stone and said: 'O Allah, if what this monk says is true, then I ask You to let me kill this animal; and if what the soothsayer says is true, then I ask You not to let me kill it.' Then he threw the stone and killed the animal. The people said: 'Who killed it?' They were told: 'The youth.' The people were astonished and said: 'This youth has knowledge that no one else has.' A blind man heard of this, came to him and said: 'If you restore my sight, I will give you such-and-such.' The youth said: 'I do not want that from you, but tell me: if your sight is returned to you, will you believe in the One who returned it to you?' He said: 'Yes.' So the youth prayed to Allah and He restored the man's sight, and the blind man believed.

"The king was informed of their affair, so he sent for them and brought them before him, and said: 'I will kill each one of you with a killing by which I will not kill his companion.' He ordered the monk and the man who had been blind to be brought, and a saw was placed on the middle of the head of one of them, and it killed him; the other was killed by another means. Then he ordered the youth and said: 'Take him to such-and-such mountain and throw him down from its peak.' They took him to that mountain, and when they reached the place from which they wanted to throw him, they began to fall down from the mountain and perish, until none of them remained except the youth. Then the youth returned, and the king ordered that they take him to the sea and throw him into it. They took him to the sea, and Allah drowned those who were with him and saved him. The youth said to the king: 'You will not kill me until you crucify me and shoot me, and say when you shoot me: In the name of Allah, the Lord of the youth.' So he ordered that he be crucified, then shot him and said: 'In the name of Allah, the Lord of the youth.' The arrow struck his temple, so the youth placed his hand on the place of the arrow, and then he died. The people said: 'This youth has knowledge that no one has had. We believe in the Lord of this youth.' It was said to the king: 'Are you anxious that three people have opposed you? Indeed, this whole world has opposed you.' He said: 'He dug a trench (ukhdud) and set in it firewood and fire. Then he gathered the people and said: Whoever recants his religion, we will leave him alone; and whoever does not recant, we will throw him into this fire.' He began to throw them into that trench. He said: 'Allah says: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel﴾, until He reached: ﴿the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾.'"

As for the youth, he was buried, then he was exhumed, and it is mentioned that he was exhumed in the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, with his finger on his temple just as he had placed it when he was killed.

The wordings of this story differ in some respects.

Muslim narrated it at the end of his Sahih from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb.

Ahmad narrated it through Affan, from Hammad, with the same chain.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan and Abd ibn Humayd, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Thabit, with the same chain.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding His saying ﴿the companions of the trench﴾, that he said: "They are the Abyssinians (al-Habashah)."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "They were people from the Children of Israel who dug a trench in the earth and kindled a fire in it, then they stood over that trench with men and women, and they were presented before it."

Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated, and he declared it sound, from Ibn Mas'ud that he said, regarding ﴿By the sky with its constellations﴾ up to His saying ﴿and a witness and a witnessed﴾: "This is an oath concerning ﴿Indeed, the seizing of your Lord is severe﴾ to the end of the surah."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats﴾, that he said: "He originates the punishment and repeats it."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying al-Wadud, that he said: "The Beloved," and regarding His saying ﴿Owner of the Throne, the Glorious﴾, that he said: "The Generous."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him, regarding His saying ﴿in a preserved tablet﴾, that he said: "I have been informed that it is the Tablet of Remembrance, a single tablet containing the Remembrance, and that this tablet is of light, and that its length is three hundred years' journey."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Anas that he said: "The Preserved Tablet which Allah mentioned in His saying ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an﴾ ﴿in a preserved tablet﴾ is on the forehead of Israfil."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated, and al-Suyuti said with a good chain, from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Allah created the Preserved Tablet, the distance of a hundred years' journey. He said to the Pen, before He created the creation: 'Write My knowledge into My creation.' So what is to occur until the Day of Resurrection has come to pass." End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 85, verse 11–22 (part 1 of 3):

Ibn al-Duraysi, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Wa-al-sama'i dhati al-buruj" was revealed in Makkah.

Ahmad related: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Zurayq ibn Abi Sulma narrated to us, Abu al-Muhazzam narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite in the late night prayer (al-'Isha' al-akhirah) "Wa-al-sama'i dhati al-buruj" and "Wa-al-sama'i wa-al-tariq"."

al-Tayalisi, Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, Ahmad, al-Darimi, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Jabir ibn Samurah: "that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers "Wa-al-sama'i wa-al-tariq" and "Wa-al-sama'i dhati al-buruj"."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: ﴿By the sky containing the buruj﴾. The discussion of al-buruj has already preceded at the explanation of His saying: ﴿He has placed in the sky buruj﴾ [al-Furqan: 61]. al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: they are the stars, and the meaning is: "By the sky containing the stars."

'Ikrimah and Mujahid also said: they are palaces in the sky.

al-Minhal ibn 'Amr said: "containing a good creation."

Abu 'Ubaydah, Yahya ibn Salam and others said: they are the stations (manazil) for the planets, and they are twelve buruj for twelve planets: Aries (al-Hamal), Taurus (al-Thawr), Gemini (al-Jawza'), Cancer (al-Saratan), Leo (al-Asad), Virgo (al-Sunbulah), Libra (al-Mizan), Scorpio (al-'Aqrab), Sagittarius (al-Qaws), Capricorn (al-Jadi), Aquarius (al-Dalw), and Pisces (al-Hut).

In the language of the Arabs, al-buruj means palaces, and from it is His saying: ﴿Even if you were in towers built up high﴾ [al-Nisa': 78]. The stations of these stars were likened to palaces because they dwell in them. It was said: they are the gates of the sky. It was said: they are the stations of the moon. The origin of al-burj is manifestation, (p-1604) and they were named so because of their visibility.

And "the promised day" means the day that was promised, which is the Day of Resurrection.

al-Wahidi said: according to the saying of all the exegetes, "witness and witnessed": the witness (al-shahid) is whoever attends on that day from among the creatures, i.e., who is present therein, and the witnessed (al-mashhud) is what is witnessed on that day of wonders. A group of the Companions and the Successors held that the witness is the day of Friday, and that it bears witness over every doer for what he did therein, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah, because people witness the Hajj season therein and the angels attend it.

al-Wahidi said: this is the saying of the majority.

al-Qushayri related from Ibn 'Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr that the witness is the day of al-Adha.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: the witness is the day of al-Tarwiyah, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah.

al-Nakha'i said: the witness is the day of 'Arafah, and the witnessed is the day of al-Nahr. It was also said: the witness is Allah, Glorified is He.

al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said this, citing His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as witness﴾ [al-Fath: 28], and His saying: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest as testimony?" Say: "Allah is witness between me and you"﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. It was also said: the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), citing His saying: ﴿So how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these?﴾ [al-Nisa': 41], and His saying: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ [al-Ahzab: 45], and His saying: ﴿And the Messenger will be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. It was also said: the witness is all the prophets, citing His saying: ﴿So how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness﴾. It was also said: it is Jesus son of Mary, citing His saying: ﴿And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 117]. The witnessed, according to these three sayings, is either the nation of Muhammad, or the nations of the prophets, or the nation of Jesus.

It was said: the witness is Adam and the witnessed is his offspring.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: the witness is the human being, citing His saying: ﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra': 14]. Mujahid said: its limbs, citing His saying: ﴿On the Day when their tongues and their hands and their feet will testify against them as to what they used to do﴾ [al-Nur: 24]. al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: the witness is this nation, and the witnessed is the rest of the nations, citing His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. It was said: the witness is the guardian angels (al-hafazah) and the witnessed is the children of Adam. It was said: the days and nights.

It was said: the witness is the creation, who bear witness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of His oneness, and the one witnessed to as One is Allah, Glorified is He. The explanation of what has come in the interpretation of the witness and the witnessed, and the statement of what is the truth, will come, Allah willing.

﴿The companions of the trench were killed﴾. This is the response to the oath, and the lam in it is implied, and this is the apparent view; al-Farra' and others held this. It was said its estimate is: "Indeed, were killed," so the lam and "qad" were omitted, and on this the sentence is informative. The apparent view is that it is supplicatory (du'a'iyyah), because the meaning of "qutila" is "la'ana" (was cursed).

al-Wahidi said: according to the consensus, and a supplicatory sentence cannot be the response to an oath. It was said the response is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who tormented the believing men and believing women...﴾. It was said it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾, and this is the view of al-Mubarrad, though it was objected to on account of the long separation. It was said it is an estimated clause indicated by His saying "qutila ashab al-ukhdud," as if He said: "I swear by these things that the disbelievers of Quraysh are cursed as the companions of the trench were cursed." It was said the estimate of the response is: "You will surely be resurrected," and Ibn al-Anbari chose this.

Abu Hatim al-Sijistani and also Ibn al-Anbari said: there is inversion and displacement in the speech: i.e., "The companions of the trench were killed, and [by] the sky containing the buruj." This was objected to on the ground that it is not permissible to say: "By Allah, Zayd stood."

al-Ukhdud: a great long cleft in the earth like a trench; its plural is akhadid. From it comes al-khadd (cheek), for the channels of tears, and al-mikhaddah (pillow), because the cheek is placed upon it. It is said "takhadadda wajh al-rajul" when furrows of boils appear in a man's face. From it is the saying of Tarafah:

"And a face as if the sun had cast its garment upon it, clear of complexion, not furrowed."

The explanation of the hadith of the companions of the trench will come, Allah willing.

The majority read "al-nari dhati al-waqud" with the genitive "al-nar," as a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimal) from "al-ukhdud," because the trench includes it. "Dhat al-waqud" is an adjective of it, that it is a great fire. al-Waqud is the firewood with which it is kindled. It was said it is a substitute of whole from whole (badal kull min kull), not a substitute of inclusion.

It was said that "al-nar" is in the genitive by attraction (al-jiwar); thus Makki related from the Kufans.

The majority read the waw in "al-waqud" with a fatha, while Qatadah, Abu Raja' and Nasr ibn 'Asim read it with a damma.

Ashhab al-'Uqayli, Abu Haywah, Abu al-Simak al-'Adawi, Ibn al-Sumayfa' and 'Isa read "al-nar" in the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject: i.e., "it is the fire," or as the subject of an omitted verb: i.e., "the fire burned them."

﴿When they were sitting over it﴾. The operator of the adverbial phrase is "qutila": i.e., they were cursed when they encircled the fire, sitting at what is close to it and near to it.

Muqatil said: meaning, sitting near the fire, presenting them with disbelief.

Mujahid said: they were sitting on chairs beside the trench.

﴿And they, of what they did to the believers, were witnesses﴾: i.e., those who dug the trench, who were the king and his companions, were witnesses to what they did to the believers of presenting them to the fire so that they would return to their religion. "Witnesses" means present, or some of them bear witness to others before the king that he did not fall short in what he was commanded.

It was said they bear witness to what they did on the Day of Resurrection, then their tongues, hands and feet will testify against them.

It was said "ala" is in the sense of "ma'a" (with), and the estimate is: "and they, with what they did to the believers, were witnesses."

al-Zajjaj said: Allah informed of the story of a people whose insight and true faith reached the point that they endured being burned with fire for the sake of Allah.

﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾: i.e., they did not object to them nor find fault with them except that they affirmed belief in Allah, the Victorious, the One praised in every state.

al-Zajjaj said: they did not object to them for any sin except their faith. This is like His saying: ﴿Do you resent us except that we believed in Allah﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 59]. This is an emphasis of praise by means of what resembles blame, as in the saying of the poet:

"There is no fault in them except that the guest with them / is distant from family, homeland and kin."

And another said:

"There is no fault in her except the squint of her eye, / as with the noble birds, the squint of whose eyes is their beauty."

al-Jumhur read "naqamu" with a fatha on the nun, while Abu Haywah read it with a kasra, and the eloquent is the fatha.

Then Glorified is He described Himself with what indicates greatness and majesty, saying: ﴿To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. And whoever has this status is worthy that He be believed in and made one. ﴿And Allah, over all things, is Witness﴾ — regarding their deeds against the believers (p-1605) — nothing is hidden from Him. In this is a severe warning for the companions of the trench, and a promise of good for those believers among them whom they tormented for their religion.

Then Glorified is He explained what He prepared for those who did to the believers what they did of burning, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who tormented the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the burning fire﴾: i.e., they burned them with fire. The Arabs say: "fatantu al-shay'," i.e., I burned it, and "fatantu al-dirham wa-al-dinar" when you put them into fire to see their quality. It is said "dinar maftun," and the goldsmith is called "al-fattan." From it is His saying: ﴿The Day they will be tried over the fire﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 13], i.e., they will be burned. It was also said the meaning of "fatanu al-mu'minin" is they tested them in their religion so that they would turn away from it; "then they did not repent" of their foul deed and turn back from their disbelief and their tormenting; "for them is the punishment of Hell": i.e., for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of Hell because of their disbelief. The sentence is in the place of nominative, as the predicate of "inna," or the predicate is "lahum," and "adhab Jahannam" is raised by it as agent. The fa' is for the subject containing the meaning of a condition. Its abrogation by "inna" does not harm, contrary to al-Akhfash. "And for them is the punishment of the burning": i.e., and for them is another punishment in addition to the punishment of their disbelief, which is the punishment of the burning that they inflicted upon the believers. It was said "al-Hariq" is one of the names of the fire, like "al-Sa'ir." It was said they will be punished in Hell with the zamharir (extreme cold), then they will be punished with the punishment of the burning; the first is punishment by its cold, and the second is punishment by its heat.

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: the punishment of the burning, they were afflicted with it in this world, because the fire rose from the trench to the king and his companions and burned them. al-Kalbi also said this.

Then He mentioned what He prepared for the believers who were burned with fire, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. The apparent meaning of the verse is generality, so those burned in the trench for their faith enter into it first and foremost. The meaning is: those who combine faith and righteous deeds ﴿will have gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: i.e., for them, because of faith and righteous deed, are gardens characterized by this attribute.

The manner in which rivers flow beneath the gardens has already been mentioned in more than one place, and we clarified that if "gardens" is meant as trees, then the flowing of rivers beneath them is clear; and if it is meant as the land containing them, then "beneath" is with regard to its visible part, which is the trees, since they cover its courtyard. The reference in His saying "that" is to what has been mentioned before of what Allah prepared for them: i.e., that mentioned is the great triumph, to which no triumph is equal, nor close, nor near. "Triumph" is attaining the sought-after object.

The sentence ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾ is a resumed sentence addressed to the Prophet (ﷺ), explaining what is with Allah, Glorified is He, of recompense for those who disobey Him and forgiveness for those who obey Him: i.e., His seizing of the tyrants and oppressors is severe. Al-batsh is seizing with force, and describing it with severity indicates that it has increased and intensified. A similar statement is His saying: ﴿Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ [Hud: 102].

﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats﴾: i.e., He creates first in this world and restores them alive after death.

Thus said the majority. It was said He originates for the disbelievers the punishment of the burning in this world, then repeats it for them in the Hereafter; Ibn Jarir chose this, but the first is more preferable.

﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Loving﴾: i.e., abundant in forgiveness for the sins of His believing servants, not disgracing them with them; abundant in love for the obedient among His friends.

Mujahid said: "al-wadud" is the one who loves His friends, so it is fa'ul in the sense of fa'il.

Ibn Zayd said: The meaning of al-Wadud is the Merciful.

Al-Mubarrad related from Isma'il al-Qadi that al-Wadud is the one who has no child, and he recited:

"And I ride in the battle, a naked woman, [on a horse] of subdued wing, a mare, a barren one (wadud)."

That is, she has no child for whom she yearns.

It was also said that al-Wadud is in the sense of al-mawdud (the one who is loved): that is, His righteous servants love Him and hold Him dear. So said al-Azhari. He said: "It is also permissible that fa'ul be in the sense of fa'il, meaning that He is loving toward them."

He said: "Both attributes are praise, for if Exalted is His remembrance loves His obedient servants, it is an act of grace from Him; and if His knowing servants love Him, it is because of the generous kindness they have come to recognize from Him."

The majority (al-Jumhur) read "dhu al-'arsh al-majid" with the majid in the nominative (raf'), as an adjective (na't) of "dhu." Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose this reading, and both said: "Because majd (glory) is the utmost in generosity and bounty, and Allah, glorified is He, is the one described by it."

The Kufans, except 'Asim, read it in the genitive (jarr), as an adjective of al-'arsh (the Throne).

He, glorified is He, has described His Throne with generosity (karam), as in the end of Surat al-Mu'minun.

It was also said that it is an adjective of Rabbika (your Lord), and the separation between them does no harm, since they are attributes of Allah, glorified is He.

Makki said: it is a predicate after a predicate, but the first is preferable.

The meaning of "dhu al-'arsh" is "possessor of dominion and authority," as one says: "So-and-so is on the throne of his kingdom." From this is the poet's saying:

"They saw my throne with its two sides broken, and when it was broken, they isolated me."

And the saying of another:

"If they kill you, their thrones have been struck down, by 'Utayba ibn al-Harith ibn Shihab."

It was also said that the intended meaning is the Creator of the Throne.

"Fa'alun li-ma yurid" (Doer of what He intends): that is, of beginning and returning (of creation).

'Ata said: He is not incapable of anything He wills, and nothing He seeks is withheld from Him. The nominative of fa'alun is by being the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada').

Al-Farra' said: it is in the nominative by repetition and resumption (al-tikrar wa'l-istinaf), since it is an absolutely indefinite noun (nakira mahda).

Ibn Jarir said: the nominative of fa'alun, which is an absolutely indefinite noun, is in agreement with the case of al-Ghafur al-Wadud. He said "fa'alun" because what He wills and does is in the utmost abundance.

Then He, glorified is He, mentioned the report of the disbelieving hosts, saying: "Has there come to you the report of the armies?" The sentence is independent (mustanafa), confirming what preceded of the severity of His seizing, glorified is He, and of His being a Doer of what He intends. In it is consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that is, "Has there come to you, O Muhammad, the report of the disbelieving hosts, who denied their prophets and were arrayed against them?"

Then He specified them, saying: "Pharaoh and Thamud." It is a substitution (badal) for "the armies."

By Pharaoh is meant him and his people, and by Thamud is meant the well-known people. By their report is meant what occurred from them of disbelief and obstinacy, and what befell them of punishment. Their story is well known and its mention has been repeated in the Mighty Book in more than one place. He limited it to these two groups because their matter is famous among the People of the Book and among the polytheist Arabs, and by them He pointed to their likes.

Then He turned away from comparing these disbelievers existing in his time (ﷺ) to those previously mentioned, and made clear that they are worse than them in disbelief and denial, saying: "Nay, those who disbelieve are in denial." That is: nay, these polytheists among the Arabs are in severe denial of you and of what you have brought, and they have not taken warning from those disbelievers who came before them.

"And Allah encompasses them from behind them" (Allah is encompassing of them from behind them): that is, He is able to bring upon them what He brought upon those. Encompassing (ihata) a thing is restraining it from all its sides, so this is a figure of speech for their not escaping, since the one encompassed cannot get away from the one encompassing.

Then He, glorified is He, returned their denial of the Qur'an, saying: "Nay, it is a Glorious Qur'an" (Qur'anun majid): that is, supremely exalted in nobility, generosity and blessing, for it is an exposition of what Allah has legislated for His servants of the rulings of the religion and of this world, and it is not, as they say, poetry, soothsaying, or magic.

"In a Preserved Tablet" (fi lawhin mahfuz): that is, written on a tablet, which is the Mother of the Book, preserved with Allah from the reach of the devils.

The majority read "mahfuzin" in the genitive, as an adjective of "lawh." Nafi' read it in the nominative, as an adjective of "al-Qur'an": that is, "Nay, it is a Glorious Qur'an preserved in a tablet."

The reciters agreed on the fatha of the lam in "lawh," except Yahya ibn Ya'mar and Ibn al-Sumayfa', who read it with a damma.

Muqatil said: the Preserved Tablet is on the right of the Throne.

It was said that by "al-lawh" with a damma on the lam is meant the air above the seventh heaven.

Abu al-Fadl said: "al-luh" with a damma on the lam is air, and Ibn Khalawayh said likewise.

In al-Sihah he said: "al-luh" with a damma is the air between the heaven and the earth.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The buruj are palaces in the sky."

Ibn Mardawayh related from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about "the sky of the buruj," and he said: "The stars." He was asked about His saying: "Who has placed in the sky buruj" [al-Furqan: 61], and he said: "The stars." And about His saying: "In towers built up" [al-Nisa': 78], and he said: "Palaces."

Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "And the promised day, and witness and witnessed" [al-Buruj: 2–3], that he said: "The promised day is the Day of Resurrection; the witness is the Day of Friday (Jumu'a); the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa, and it is the Greater Hajj. The Day of Friday, Allah made it a festival for Muhammad and his Ummah, and preferred them thereby over all creation; it is the master of days with Allah, and the most beloved of deeds to Allah are done on it. In it is an hour in which no Muslim servant who prays and asks Allah for good will coincide with it, except that He gives him it."

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witnessed day is the Day of 'Arafa, and the witness is the Day of Friday. The sun has not risen nor set upon a day better than it. In it is an hour in which no believing servant coincides with it, asking Allah for good, except that Allah answers him; and he does not seek refuge from anything except that He protects him from it."

al-Hakim related and authenticated, as did Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi, from Abu Hurayra, raising it: "'And witness and witnessed': he said: The witness is the Day of 'Arafa and the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the promised one, the Day of Resurrection."

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib who said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witnessed is the Day of Sacrifice (al-nahr), and the witness is the Day of Friday.

Ibn Jarir and al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh related by the route of Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witness is the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa."

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related from Jubayr ibn Mut'im who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning the verse: "The witness is the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa."

'Abd ibn Humayd related the like from Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Hurayra as a mawquf (companion's) report.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the master of days is Friday, and it is the witness, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa." This is a mursal report from the mursal reports of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.

Ibn Majah, al-Tabarani and Ibn Jarir related from Abu al-Darda' who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Increase your sending of blessings upon me on the Day of Friday, for it is a witnessed day, which the angels witness."

'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib regarding the verse that he said: The witness is the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali that a man asked him about His saying: "And witness and witnessed," and he said: "Have you asked anyone before me?" He said: "Yes, I asked Ibn 'Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr, and they said: the Day of Sacrifice and the Day of Friday." He said: "No, but the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ)," then he recited: "And We bring you as a witness over these" [al-Nisa': 41]; "and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection," then he recited: "That is a day on which mankind will be gathered, and that is a witnessed day" [Hud: 103].

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and al-Saghir, and Ibn Mardawayh related from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali regarding the verse that he said: The witness is my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection; then he recited: "Indeed We have sent you as a witness" [al-Ahzab: 45], and "That is a witnessed day."

'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir related by various routes from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection; then he recited: "That is a day on which mankind will be gathered, and that is a witnessed day" [Hud: 103]. Ibn Jarir also related from him: The witness is Allah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: The witness is Allah.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him also: The witness is Allah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

I say: These interpretations from the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, have differed, as you see, and likewise the interpretations of the Successors after them differed. Those among them who relied upon verses in which Allah mentions that a thing is a witness or witnessed took that as evidence that this is what is meant by "witness" and "witnessed" in this absolute verse. But that is not an argument by which it is established that the witness and witnessed mentioned in this context are that witness and witnessed mentioned in another verse; otherwise it would follow that His saying here "witness and witnessed" means everything to which the Mighty Book or the Pure Sunna has applied the description of being witnessed or witnessing, and none of what they cited, despite their differing, is more deserving than another, and no one has said so.

If you say: Does the raised report that you mentioned, from the two hadiths of Abu Hurayra, the hadith of Abu Malik, the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im, and the mursal of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, specify this promised day and the witness and witnessed? I say: As for the promised day, these reports which mention it do not differ; rather they agree that it is the Day of Resurrection. As for the witness, in the first hadith of Abu Hurayra it is the Day of Friday; in his second hadith it is the Day of Friday; in the mursal of Sa'id it is the Day of Friday; in his second hadith it is the Day of 'Arafa and the Day of Friday; in the hadith of Abu Malik it is the Day of Friday; in the hadith of Jubayr it is the Day of Friday; in the mursal of Sa'id it is the Day of Friday. These hadiths thus agree upon it, and the addition of the Day of 'Arafa to it in the second hadith of Abu Hurayra does no harm. As for the witnessed, in the first hadith of Abu Hurayra it is the Day of 'Arafa; in his second hadith it is the Day of Resurrection; in the hadith of Abu Malik it is the Day of 'Arafa; in the hadith of Jubayr it is the Day of 'Arafa; likewise in the hadith of Sa'id. Thus it has become determined in these reports that it is the Day of 'Arafa, and these are more preferred than that report in which it is stated to be the Day of Resurrection. From the totality of this results the preference of what the majority of the Companions, the Successors and those after them held: that the witness is the Day of Friday and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafa. As for the promised day, we have already mentioned that consensus has occurred that it is the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 85, verses 11–22 (part 3 of 3):

Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and al-Tabarani narrated from Suhayb that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There was a king among those who came before you, and this king had a soothsayer (kahin) who foretold for him. The soothsayer said to him: 'Look for me a youth who is intelligent and quick-witted, and I will teach him my knowledge, for I fear that I will die and this knowledge will be cut off from you, and there will be no one among you who knows it.' So they searched for a youth fitting his description, and they ordered him to attend the soothsayer and to visit him regularly. The youth kept visiting him. On the youth's path there was a monk (rahib) in a hermitage (sawma'ah), so the youth would ask that monk whenever he passed by him, until the monk informed him. The monk said: 'I only worship Allah.' The youth began to linger with this monk and to be late for the soothsayer, so the soothsayer sent to the youth's family that he was hardly ever present with him. The youth informed the monk of this, and the monk said to him: 'When he asks you, Where were you? say, With my family; and when your family asks you, Where were you? tell them, I was with the soothsayer.'

"While the youth was in this state, he passed by a large crowd of people who had been held up by an animal, which it is said was a lion. The youth took a stone and said: 'O Allah, if what this monk says is true, then I ask You to let me kill this animal; and if what the soothsayer says is true, then I ask You not to let me kill it.' Then he threw the stone and killed the animal. The people said: 'Who killed it?' They were told: 'The youth.' The people were astonished and said: 'This youth has knowledge that no one else has.' A blind man heard of this, came to him and said: 'If you restore my sight, I will give you such-and-such.' The youth said: 'I do not want that from you, but tell me: if your sight is returned to you, will you believe in the One who returned it to you?' He said: 'Yes.' So the youth prayed to Allah and He restored the man's sight, and the blind man believed.

"The king was informed of their affair, so he sent for them and brought them before him, and said: 'I will kill each one of you with a killing by which I will not kill his companion.' He ordered the monk and the man who had been blind to be brought, and a saw was placed on the middle of the head of one of them, and it killed him; the other was killed by another means. Then he ordered the youth and said: 'Take him to such-and-such mountain and throw him down from its peak.' They took him to that mountain, and when they reached the place from which they wanted to throw him, they began to fall down from the mountain and perish, until none of them remained except the youth. Then the youth returned, and the king ordered that they take him to the sea and throw him into it. They took him to the sea, and Allah drowned those who were with him and saved him. The youth said to the king: 'You will not kill me until you crucify me and shoot me, and say when you shoot me: In the name of Allah, the Lord of the youth.' So he ordered that he be crucified, then shot him and said: 'In the name of Allah, the Lord of the youth.' The arrow struck his temple, so the youth placed his hand on the place of the arrow, and then he died. The people said: 'This youth has knowledge that no one has had. We believe in the Lord of this youth.' It was said to the king: 'Are you anxious that three people have opposed you? Indeed, this whole world has opposed you.' He said: 'He dug a trench (ukhdud) and set in it firewood and fire. Then he gathered the people and said: Whoever recants his religion, we will leave him alone; and whoever does not recant, we will throw him into this fire.' He began to throw them into that trench. He said: 'Allah says: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel﴾, until He reached: ﴿the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾.'"

As for the youth, he was buried, then he was exhumed, and it is mentioned that he was exhumed in the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, with his finger on his temple just as he had placed it when he was killed.

The wordings of this story differ in some respects.

Muslim narrated it at the end of his Sahih from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb.

Ahmad narrated it through Affan, from Hammad, with the same chain.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan and Abd ibn Humayd, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Thabit, with the same chain.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding His saying ﴿the companions of the trench﴾, that he said: "They are the Abyssinians (al-Habashah)."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "They were people from the Children of Israel who dug a trench in the earth and kindled a fire in it, then they stood over that trench with men and women, and they were presented before it."

Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim narrated, and he declared it sound, from Ibn Mas'ud that he said, regarding ﴿By the sky with its constellations﴾ up to His saying ﴿and a witness and a witnessed﴾: "This is an oath concerning ﴿Indeed, the seizing of your Lord is severe﴾ to the end of the surah."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats﴾, that he said: "He originates the punishment and repeats it."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying al-Wadud, that he said: "The Beloved," and regarding His saying ﴿Owner of the Throne, the Glorious﴾, that he said: "The Generous."

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him, regarding His saying ﴿in a preserved tablet﴾, that he said: "I have been informed that it is the Tablet of Remembrance, a single tablet containing the Remembrance, and that this tablet is of light, and that its length is three hundred years' journey."

Ibn Jarir narrated from Anas that he said: "The Preserved Tablet which Allah mentioned in His saying ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an﴾ ﴿in a preserved tablet﴾ is on the forehead of Israfil."

Abu al-Shaykh narrated, and al-Suyuti said with a good chain, from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Allah created the Preserved Tablet, the distance of a hundred years' journey. He said to the Pen, before He created the creation: 'Write My knowledge into My creation.' So what is to occur until the Day of Resurrection has come to pass." End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 85, verse 11–22 (part 1 of 3):

Ibn al-Duraysi, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Wa-al-sama'i dhati al-buruj" was revealed in Makkah.

Ahmad related: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Zurayq ibn Abi Sulma narrated to us, Abu al-Muhazzam narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite in the late night prayer (al-'Isha' al-akhirah) "Wa-al-sama'i dhati al-buruj" and "Wa-al-sama'i wa-al-tariq"."

al-Tayalisi, Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, Ahmad, al-Darimi, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Jabir ibn Samurah: "that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite in the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers "Wa-al-sama'i wa-al-tariq" and "Wa-al-sama'i dhati al-buruj"."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: ﴿By the sky containing the buruj﴾. The discussion of al-buruj has already preceded at the explanation of His saying: ﴿He has placed in the sky buruj﴾ [al-Furqan: 61]. al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: they are the stars, and the meaning is: "By the sky containing the stars."

'Ikrimah and Mujahid also said: they are palaces in the sky.

al-Minhal ibn 'Amr said: "containing a good creation."

Abu 'Ubaydah, Yahya ibn Salam and others said: they are the stations (manazil) for the planets, and they are twelve buruj for twelve planets: Aries (al-Hamal), Taurus (al-Thawr), Gemini (al-Jawza'), Cancer (al-Saratan), Leo (al-Asad), Virgo (al-Sunbulah), Libra (al-Mizan), Scorpio (al-'Aqrab), Sagittarius (al-Qaws), Capricorn (al-Jadi), Aquarius (al-Dalw), and Pisces (al-Hut).

In the language of the Arabs, al-buruj means palaces, and from it is His saying: ﴿Even if you were in towers built up high﴾ [al-Nisa': 78]. The stations of these stars were likened to palaces because they dwell in them. It was said: they are the gates of the sky. It was said: they are the stations of the moon. The origin of al-burj is manifestation, (p-1604) and they were named so because of their visibility.

And "the promised day" means the day that was promised, which is the Day of Resurrection.

al-Wahidi said: according to the saying of all the exegetes, "witness and witnessed": the witness (al-shahid) is whoever attends on that day from among the creatures, i.e., who is present therein, and the witnessed (al-mashhud) is what is witnessed on that day of wonders. A group of the Companions and the Successors held that the witness is the day of Friday, and that it bears witness over every doer for what he did therein, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah, because people witness the Hajj season therein and the angels attend it.

al-Wahidi said: this is the saying of the majority.

al-Qushayri related from Ibn 'Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr that the witness is the day of al-Adha.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: the witness is the day of al-Tarwiyah, and the witnessed is the day of 'Arafah.

al-Nakha'i said: the witness is the day of 'Arafah, and the witnessed is the day of al-Nahr. It was also said: the witness is Allah, Glorified is He.

al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said this, citing His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as witness﴾ [al-Fath: 28], and His saying: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest as testimony?" Say: "Allah is witness between me and you"﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. It was also said: the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), citing His saying: ﴿So how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these?﴾ [al-Nisa': 41], and His saying: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ [al-Ahzab: 45], and His saying: ﴿And the Messenger will be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. It was also said: the witness is all the prophets, citing His saying: ﴿So how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness﴾. It was also said: it is Jesus son of Mary, citing His saying: ﴿And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 117]. The witnessed, according to these three sayings, is either the nation of Muhammad, or the nations of the prophets, or the nation of Jesus.

It was said: the witness is Adam and the witnessed is his offspring.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: the witness is the human being, citing His saying: ﴿Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra': 14]. Mujahid said: its limbs, citing His saying: ﴿On the Day when their tongues and their hands and their feet will testify against them as to what they used to do﴾ [al-Nur: 24]. al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: the witness is this nation, and the witnessed is the rest of the nations, citing His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a median nation that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. It was said: the witness is the guardian angels (al-hafazah) and the witnessed is the children of Adam. It was said: the days and nights.

It was said: the witness is the creation, who bear witness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of His oneness, and the one witnessed to as One is Allah, Glorified is He. The explanation of what has come in the interpretation of the witness and the witnessed, and the statement of what is the truth, will come, Allah willing.

﴿The companions of the trench were killed﴾. This is the response to the oath, and the lam in it is implied, and this is the apparent view; al-Farra' and others held this. It was said its estimate is: "Indeed, were killed," so the lam and "qad" were omitted, and on this the sentence is informative. The apparent view is that it is supplicatory (du'a'iyyah), because the meaning of "qutila" is "la'ana" (was cursed).

al-Wahidi said: according to the consensus, and a supplicatory sentence cannot be the response to an oath. It was said the response is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who tormented the believing men and believing women...﴾. It was said it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾, and this is the view of al-Mubarrad, though it was objected to on account of the long separation. It was said it is an estimated clause indicated by His saying "qutila ashab al-ukhdud," as if He said: "I swear by these things that the disbelievers of Quraysh are cursed as the companions of the trench were cursed." It was said the estimate of the response is: "You will surely be resurrected," and Ibn al-Anbari chose this.

Abu Hatim al-Sijistani and also Ibn al-Anbari said: there is inversion and displacement in the speech: i.e., "The companions of the trench were killed, and [by] the sky containing the buruj." This was objected to on the ground that it is not permissible to say: "By Allah, Zayd stood."

al-Ukhdud: a great long cleft in the earth like a trench; its plural is akhadid. From it comes al-khadd (cheek), for the channels of tears, and al-mikhaddah (pillow), because the cheek is placed upon it. It is said "takhadadda wajh al-rajul" when furrows of boils appear in a man's face. From it is the saying of Tarafah:

"And a face as if the sun had cast its garment upon it, clear of complexion, not furrowed."

The explanation of the hadith of the companions of the trench will come, Allah willing.

The majority read "al-nari dhati al-waqud" with the genitive "al-nar," as a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimal) from "al-ukhdud," because the trench includes it. "Dhat al-waqud" is an adjective of it, that it is a great fire. al-Waqud is the firewood with which it is kindled. It was said it is a substitute of whole from whole (badal kull min kull), not a substitute of inclusion.

It was said that "al-nar" is in the genitive by attraction (al-jiwar); thus Makki related from the Kufans.

The majority read the waw in "al-waqud" with a fatha, while Qatadah, Abu Raja' and Nasr ibn 'Asim read it with a damma.

Ashhab al-'Uqayli, Abu Haywah, Abu al-Simak al-'Adawi, Ibn al-Sumayfa' and 'Isa read "al-nar" in the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject: i.e., "it is the fire," or as the subject of an omitted verb: i.e., "the fire burned them."

﴿When they were sitting over it﴾. The operator of the adverbial phrase is "qutila": i.e., they were cursed when they encircled the fire, sitting at what is close to it and near to it.

Muqatil said: meaning, sitting near the fire, presenting them with disbelief.

Mujahid said: they were sitting on chairs beside the trench.

﴿And they, of what they did to the believers, were witnesses﴾: i.e., those who dug the trench, who were the king and his companions, were witnesses to what they did to the believers of presenting them to the fire so that they would return to their religion. "Witnesses" means present, or some of them bear witness to others before the king that he did not fall short in what he was commanded.

It was said they bear witness to what they did on the Day of Resurrection, then their tongues, hands and feet will testify against them.

It was said "ala" is in the sense of "ma'a" (with), and the estimate is: "and they, with what they did to the believers, were witnesses."

al-Zajjaj said: Allah informed of the story of a people whose insight and true faith reached the point that they endured being burned with fire for the sake of Allah.

﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾: i.e., they did not object to them nor find fault with them except that they affirmed belief in Allah, the Victorious, the One praised in every state.

al-Zajjaj said: they did not object to them for any sin except their faith. This is like His saying: ﴿Do you resent us except that we believed in Allah﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 59]. This is an emphasis of praise by means of what resembles blame, as in the saying of the poet:

"There is no fault in them except that the guest with them / is distant from family, homeland and kin."

And another said:

"There is no fault in her except the squint of her eye, / as with the noble birds, the squint of whose eyes is their beauty."

al-Jumhur read "naqamu" with a fatha on the nun, while Abu Haywah read it with a kasra, and the eloquent is the fatha.

Then Glorified is He described Himself with what indicates greatness and majesty, saying: ﴿To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. And whoever has this status is worthy that He be believed in and made one. ﴿And Allah, over all things, is Witness﴾ — regarding their deeds against the believers (p-1605) — nothing is hidden from Him. In this is a severe warning for the companions of the trench, and a promise of good for those believers among them whom they tormented for their religion.

Then Glorified is He explained what He prepared for those who did to the believers what they did of burning, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who tormented the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the burning fire﴾: i.e., they burned them with fire. The Arabs say: "fatantu al-shay'," i.e., I burned it, and "fatantu al-dirham wa-al-dinar" when you put them into fire to see their quality.
